source: Old Notion page 'TCP, UDP, and IP: the transport foundations' (3c65c17b0d0d8117b21dcb9041879564), saved verbatim by the root at ../../src/read/old/tcp_udp_ip.md. Treated as unverified notes; every fact checked 2026-10-05.
verdicts: verified = checked against the source named and carried; corrected = old text wrong or stale, correction carried; unconfirmed = not carried; sibling = owned by another child page

facts.old: Best resources: HPBN Building Blocks of TCP, ESnet host tuning, RFC 9293 and man 7 tcp, EC2 bandwidth and MTU docs, NCCL env vars
facts.verdict: verified (links checked)

facts.old: IPv4 32-bit, 20-byte header, routers may fragment; IPv6 128-bit, 40-byte header, no checksum, routers never fragment
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 791, RFC 8200)

facts.old: RFC 1918 ranges
facts.verdict: verified

facts.old: CGNAT 100.64/10 (RFC 6598) collides with VPC/overlay ranges
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 6598)

facts.old: 169.254.169.254 is EC2 metadata; SSRF link to DNS page
facts.verdict: verified (AWS IMDS doc)

facts.old: Google IPv6 crossed 50% on 2026-03-28 (50.10%)
facts.verdict: verified from Google's published data file; latest 51.69% on 2026-10-03 added

facts.old: APNIC figure near 42%
facts.verdict: unconfirmed (not fetched); not carried

facts.old: MTU 1500, MSS 1460 (IPv4) / 1440 (IPv6), 12 bytes less with timestamps; IPv6 minimum 1280
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 8200 s5; arithmetic)

facts.old: PMTUD signals: ICMPv4 type 3 code 4, ICMPv6 type 2; ICMP filtering creates a black hole; connects fine, stalls on bulk
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 1191, RFC 8201); measured the ICMP 'frag needed' message on this laptop's path (MTU 1492)

facts.old: tcp_mtu_probing=1 enables PLPMTUD (RFC 4821)
facts.verdict: verified (ip-sysctl: 0 default, 1 on black hole, 2 always)

facts.old: AWS jumbo 9001 on current-generation instances, inside VPC, placement groups, Direct Connect; not via internet gateway (1500) or VPN
facts.verdict: verified (EC2 network MTU doc)

facts.old: Inter-region peering and NAT gateways cap at 8500
facts.verdict: corrected: current doc lists 8500 only for inter-region VPC peering; no NAT gateway figure

facts.old: About six times fewer packets at 9001
facts.verdict: verified by arithmetic (8949/1448 = 6.18)

facts.old: Jumbo frames irrelevant on EFA/RDMA paths that bypass kernel IP
facts.verdict: not carried as stated (no source for the 'irrelevant' claim); EFA OS-bypass verified

facts.old: ping -M do -s 8973 to test 9001
facts.verdict: verified by arithmetic

facts.old: Mixed-MTU failure: small collectives fine, large allreduce hangs; verify MTU uniformity
facts.verdict: carried as mechanism (follows from MTU rules)

facts.old: NAT gateway: 55,000 simultaneous connections per unique destination per IP; scales to 100 Gbps and 10M pps; idle 350 s
facts.verdict: verified (NAT gateway basics; troubleshooting: 350 s then RST)

facts.old: 500 dataloader workers through NAT hit ErrorPortAllocation; use S3 gateway endpoint, removes data-processing charge
facts.verdict: metric verified (CloudWatch doc); gateway endpoint 'no additional charge' verified; the 500-worker figure is illustrative and not carried

facts.old: Throughput is window over RTT
facts.verdict: verified and measured (12 real downloads)

facts.old: BDP table 125 MB / 3.1 MB / 625 KB
facts.verdict: verified by arithmetic

facts.old: 16-bit window: about 5 Mbps at 100 ms without window scaling; scaling negotiated in SYN only; middlebox stripping reimposes 64 KB
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 7323; 5.2 Mbit/s derived)

facts.old: Mathis: about 37 Mbps at MSS 1460, 100 ms, p=1e-5
facts.verdict: corrected: 45 Mbit/s with the paper's constant sqrt(3/2)

facts.old: Window ceiling + loss + per-flow cap = argument for multi-stream
facts.verdict: verified

facts.old: Nagle plus delayed ACK: 40 ms stall per RPC on write-write-read; Linux minimum delayed ACK about 40 ms
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 896, RFC 1122 s4.2.3.2, tcp.h TCP_DELACK_MIN HZ/25); not reproducible on macOS loopback (root Failure lab)

facts.old: TCP_NODELAY default in most RPC stacks including gRPC; TCP_CORK opposite
facts.verdict: verified for gRPC (grpc_set_socket_low_latency in tcp_client_posix.cc) and Go; measured Python asyncio (server-accepted sockets left with Nagle on, on macOS)

facts.old: TIME_WAIT 60 s hardcoded; 28,232 ephemeral ports; about 470 conn/s; EADDRNOTAVAIL; fix pooling
facts.verdict: verified (tcp.h TCP_TIMEWAIT_LEN; ip-sysctl ip_local_port_range)

facts.old: tcp_tw_reuse=1 helps outbound; tcp_tw_recycle removed in 4.12
facts.verdict: verified (ip-sysctl default 2; commit 4396e46187ca in v4.12)

facts.old: SO_REUSEPORT kernel load-balances accept across workers; SO_REUSEADDR binds despite TIME_WAIT
facts.verdict: verified (man 7 socket)

facts.old: Keepalive 7200 s + 9 x 75 s = 2 h 11 min; middleboxes kill idle flows earlier; TCP_USER_TIMEOUT plus app heartbeats; keepalive cannot detect a wedged peer
facts.verdict: verified (tcp.h; man 7 tcp; AWS NAT)

facts.old: somaxconn 4096 since 5.4 (was 128); overflow silently drops ACK, 1 s and 3 s stalls; ss -lnt Recv-Q/Send-Q; nstat ListenOverflows
facts.verdict: verified and refined: Linux drops new SYNs when the accept queue is full (tcp_input.c) and ignores the final ACK unless tcp_abort_on_overflow; Recv-Q/Send-Q meaning verified in tcp_diag.c; macOS behaviour measured

facts.old: CUBIC Linux default since 2006, RFC 9438 (2023)
facts.verdict: partly verified: RFC 9438 s1 says default in Linux, Windows and Apple stacks; the year 2006 not verified, dropped

facts.old: BBR models bottleneck bandwidth and RTprop, paces; BBRv1 in mainline since 4.9
facts.verdict: verified (commit 0f8782ea1497 in v4.9)

facts.old: BBRv3 is draft-ietf-ccwg-bbr-06 (2026-07-06), not confirmed in mainline; ships via google/bbr v3 and XanMod
facts.verdict: draft status verified (Datatracker rev 06, 2026-07-06); distribution claims unconfirmed, not carried

facts.old: Head-of-line blocking; HTTP/2 multiplexing stalls all streams on a loss; motivation for QUIC
facts.verdict: verified; measured by the root's On the wire tab (linked)

facts.old: TCP Fast Open effectively dead; Firefox removed it in v87; middlebox ossification
facts.verdict: unconfirmed (Firefox release not checked); not carried. Ossification as QUIC's motivation carried generally

facts.old: UDP 8-byte header; ports, boundaries, optional checksum (mandatory in IPv6); no ordering, reliability, flow or congestion control
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 768); boundaries measured

facts.old: Max UDP payload without fragmentation 1472 / 1452
facts.verdict: verified by arithmetic

facts.old: DNS Flag Day 2020: 1232 bytes; QUIC requires 1200-byte payload and probes
facts.verdict: verified (dnsflagday.net; RFC 9000 s14; RFC 8899); 1200-byte first datagram measured

facts.old: RoCEv2 is RDMA in UDP port 4791, depends on near-lossless fabric (PFC/DCQCN)
facts.verdict: port verified (IANA); PFC/DCQCN claim not checked here, left to Training Infrastructure

facts.old: EFA uses SRD, custom OS-bypass, sprays across paths and reorders at the endpoint
facts.verdict: SRD and OS bypass verified (EFA doc); spraying and reordering not in the fetched doc, not carried

facts.old: UDP has no receive-buffer autotuning; 208 KB default too small for QUIC; quic-go recommends 7.5 MB; diagnose UdpRcvbufErrors
facts.verdict: verified and corrected: rmem_max default became 4 MB in Linux 6.18 (commit a6d4f25888b8); drops measured on loopback

facts.old: Linux knobs table (cubic, somaxconn, tcp_rmem/wmem, rmem_max caps setsockopt not autotuning, port range, tw_reuse 2, netdev_max_backlog 1000, mtu_probing, file-max/ulimit)
facts.verdict: verified against ip-sysctl and net.rst; netdev_max_backlog default and 100G recommendation not in the current doc text, not carried

facts.old: setsockopt(SO_RCVBUF) disables autotuning; tuned client slower on long path; ceilings 134217728 for 100 ms 10 Gbps
facts.verdict: verified (ip-sysctl tcp_rmem); BDP 125 MB stated

facts.old: On Slurm, limits come from slurmd's environment, not the login shell
facts.verdict: corrected: slurm.conf PropagateResourceLimits default propagates the submit shell's soft limits

facts.old: ss -tinm best command; ss -lnt; nstat; ethtool -S; mtr; iperf3 -P 8 vs -P 1
facts.verdict: verified (man 8 ss field list)

facts.old: Training-job stall checklist: wrong interface (NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME, GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME), MTU mismatch, PMTUD, retransmits, NIC drops, accept queue, fd exhaustion, security groups (all ports, not just 29500), straggler rank
facts.verdict: verified (NCCL and PyTorch docs; torchrun default port 29500 in run.py); 'all ports' softened: NCCL docs name no fixed port range

facts.old: NCCL bootstraps over TCP even on InfiniBand; transport preference NVLink, P2P/SHM, IB verbs, sockets
facts.verdict: verified (NCCL env doc: InfiniBand connection bootstrap sockets; NCCL_IB_DISABLE fallback)

facts.old: NCCL_SOCKET_NTHREADS x NCCL_NSOCKS_PERTHREAD: AWS 2 and 8 = 16; 1 and 1 elsewhere; product capped at 64
facts.verdict: verified (AWS defaults and cap); the 'elsewhere' defaults not re-read, not carried

facts.old: AWS single flow 5 Gbps, 10 in placement group, 25 with ENA Express
facts.verdict: verified (EC2 bandwidth doc; MPTCP mention added)

facts.old: 70B bf16 = 140 GB; full state approaches 1 TB; 224 s and about 27 min at 5 Gbps
facts.verdict: verified by arithmetic with 14 bytes/param: 980 GB, 1,568 s = 26 min

facts.old: torch.distributed.checkpoint gets multi-stream for free (per-rank shards); s5cmd faster than aws s3 cp
facts.verdict: DCP verified (docs); s5cmd named as a tool without the speed claim

facts.old: Small-file dataloading latency-bound; WebDataset/Parquet/MDS; S3 5,500 GET / 3,500 PUT per prefix
facts.verdict: verified (S3 performance doc)

facts.old: io_uring zero-copy receive in Linux 6.15; devmem TCP
facts.verdict: verified (iou-zcrx doc commit in v6.15; devmem doc)

facts.old: HTTP/3 about 40% of websites by August 2026
facts.verdict: verified and updated: 40.8% on W3Techs, 2026-10-05

facts.old: DPDK irrelevant to ML; eBPF/XDP for observability
facts.verdict: opinion, unsourced; not carried

facts.old: L4S RFC 9330/9331/9332, ISP deployment
facts.verdict: RFC 9330 verified; deployment claim not carried

facts.old: Connections: HTTP page, WebSocket page, DNS page, interconnect page
facts.verdict: linked (WebSocket page folded into Streaming and real-time)

counts.note: several carried facts drop an unverified detail; the verdict says which
